national.title: Residents leave devastated Russian-occupied Oleshky as evacuation corridor opens
national.summary: Several hundred people are understood to have decided to stay in the frontline town, despite the lack of gas, electricity and running water.
national.body:
The evacuation of the Russian-occupied Ukrainian city of Oleshky is under way, Russian and Ukrainian authorities have confirmed.

A ceasefire, brokered by US First Lady Melania Trump, has been in force in the entire frontline region of Kherson since Tuesday, allowing for the road out of Oleshky to be demined.

Residents of Oleshky who wished to leave had a four-hour window to do so. A convoy of 25 buses was brought in to allow up to 750 people to leave the town until 14:00 (12:00 GMT), along with ambulances for people with limited mobility.

Several hundred people are understood to have decided to stay, despite the widespread devastation and the lack of gas, electricity and running water.

"Everyone who wishes to leave Oleshky will be given the opportunity to do so safely," Ukraine's human rights ombudsman Dmytro Lubinets said.

"At the same time, those who decide to remain will be able to stay and will receive all the necessary humanitarian assistance."

Ukrainian territory lies 5km (3.1miles) from Oleshky, but the evacuees will first have to travel into Russian-occupied territory and then to the southern Russian city of Anapa.

They will board a Russian government plane to Gomel in Belarus, and then drive across the border into Ukraine's Chernihiv region.

Yet, Schindler said he felt "very good about our trajectory" with an AI-focused version of the search engine.

Google's role in answering the world's questions has been challenged by the AI boom, with millions of people using programs such as ChatGPT and Claude instead.

Shares in the company plummeted over 12% to a six-month low following the release of the results.

national.title: Sir Ian McKellen leads tributes to 'beloved actor' Sir Patrick Stewart after his death at 86
national.summary: The actor died in Los Angeles following a "a brief and poignant journey" with Alzheimer's Disease and Lewy Body Dementia.
national.body:
Sir Ian McKellen has led tributes to Sir Patrick Stewart following his death at the age of 86, calling him "the most respected and beloved actor of his generation".

Tributes to the renowned British actor have poured in since his death at his Los Angeles home after "a brief and poignant journey" with Alzheimer's disease and Lewy Body Dementia was announced on Thursday.

"He wore his heart on his sleeve, which made him a man to rely on, to admire and, in my case, love," Sir Ian, Sir Patrick's X-Men co-star, said.

Famous for his role as Captain Jean-Luc Picard in Star Trek, Sir Patrick was a versatile actor who won multiple awards, balancing Hollywood roles and a career in classical theatre.

Sir Patrick Stewart: Actor who moved effortlessly between Star Trek and Shakespeare

Published 8 hours ago William Shatner, who also helmed the USS Enterprise in Star Trek, said Sir Patrick brought "intelligence, grace and a deep sense of humanity to everything he did".

"Captain Picard stood for the best of us and so did the man who played him. I was filled with affection and admiration for him and his work," Shatner added.

Stewart depicted Picard in more than 170 episodes of the hit sci-fi TV series between 1987 and 1994, as well as in four feature films. He returned to the role for Star Trek: Picard in 2020.

national.title: Why is the Cheesecake Factory at the center of the latest culture war?
national.summary: A joke by former President Obama has gone viral and received backlash from the Trump administration as the issue of affordability looms large over next week's midterm elections.
national.body:
The Cheesecake Factory is seen on May 02, 2025 in Arlington, Virginia. Kayla Bartkowski/Getty hide caption

They say there's no such thing as bad publicity. If that's true it's been a golden week for the Cheesecake Factory restaurant chain.

The furore began when former President Obama, stumping for Democrats in Ohio this week ahead of the midterms, joked about President Trump's White House refurbishments, saying they looked "like Saddam Hussein opened a Cheesecake Factory. Just gold everywhere."

The late Iraqi dictator was known for building lavish palaces, with gold walls, cabinets of gold-plated rifles, a golden throne and of course plenty of depictions of the man himself.

Trump is also well-known for his love of anything gilded and Obama joked he'd been "supergluing gold medallions to the mantel in the Oval Office," while also paving over the Rose Garden and "building a ballroom that's bigger than the White House."

Former President Barack Obama speaks during a campaign rally for Democratic Ohio Senate candidate Sherrod Brown, Saturday, Oct. 24, 2026, in Cleveland. Sue Ogrocki/AP hide caption

And the Cheesecake Factory? The beloved U.S. restaurant chain was started in 1978 by David Overton, whose mother reportedly made a fine cheesecake, and now has 218 locations across the country and an annual revenue of $1.03 billion.

But it's as well known for its kitschy decor as its food, with The Atlantic writer Elaine Godfrey describing it in an article this week "as if ancient Egypt and Tuscany had a baby in Las Vegas."

national.summary: The November 2026 midterm elections are just four days away. Candidates in key races — and President Trump — are making their closing arguments to voters.
national.body: Why Pennsylvania could be one of last states to count ballots this Election Day With four days until Election Day, Philadelphia Mayor Cherelle Parker and city commissioners are urging people to vote. Officials on Thursday escorted the media through a warehouse in Northeast Philly known as Philadelphia Election Headquarters. Every ballot placed in the city, whether in person or by mail, ends up at the warehouse to be counted on Election Day. As mail-in ballots are returned, they are first sorted by a huge machine that separates the envelopes by ward and division. Then, they are stored securely behind locked cages and won't be touched until Tuesday. Unlike most states, Pennsylvania doesn't allow workers to start processing mail-in ballots until Election Day. Then, starting at 7 a.m., workers use heavy-duty machines known as extractors to open the envelopes, but a person has to physically remove the ballot. From there, election workers sit at long tables and flatten the ballots before they are scanned and counted. Read more here .

national.summary: A U.S.-based blockchain intelligence firm says a North Korean​ unit was likely behind the hack that impacted more than $6 billion on Binance, the world's biggest cryptocurrency exchange.
national.body: A U.S.-based blockchain intelligence firm says a North Korean unit was likely behind the hack that impacted more than $6 billion on Binance, the world's biggest cryptocurrency exchange. Binance said it worked with blockchain partners to freeze roughly $3 billion in affected assets. The cryptocurrency exchange said Friday that deposits were unaffected, while withdrawals were suspended and are expected to resume in the next day or two. It said it will cover all losses. The company said on social media Friday that an initial investigation suggested the incident may have involved a compromised laptop, but that a subsequent investigation uncovered additional "points of breach." TRM, in a post on its website Thursday, attributed the attack to TraderTraitor, which it described as North Korea's elite hacking unit. "We make this judgment with high confidence," the firm said. "An attacker moved approximately USD 6.36 billion out of Binance wallets on ten blockchains, most of it in about 20 minutes," TRM said. That would make the hack the largest cryptocurrency theft on record, it said. In February last year, another cryptocurrency exchange, Bybit, suffered a $1.5 billion hit when it was hacked. The FBI said North Korea and TraderTraitor were responsible for the hack. "Several features of this attack match earlier North Korea-linked heists, including the Bybit hack," TRM said. Blockchain analysis company Chainalysis also believed the Binance hack was "likely done by DPRK group TraderTraitor," its co-founder and CEO Jonathan Levin wrote on social media. DPRK stands for the Democratic People's Republic of Korea, North Korea's official name. Binance said on social media that its "teams are working around the clock to resolve this issue safely and thoroughly. We are working closely with our law enforcement partners to confirm the identity of these criminals and bring them to justice." Experts say North Korea has turned to crypto hacking and other illicit cyber activities as a source of badly needed foreign currency to support its troubled economy and fund its nuclear program in the wake of tough U.N. sanctions and other difficulties. national.summary: It wasn't immediately clear the extent of the damage hackers might have been able to cause, and Binance had not explicitly confirmed that funds had been pilfered. The company said its teams are "working around the clock" to resolve the issue.
national.body:
FILE - The Binance logo is seen on a smartphone, Feb. 28, 2023, in Marple Township, Pa. Matt Slocum/AP hide caption

LOS ANGELES — Binance, the world's largest cryptocurrency exchange, said Thursday it's investigating reports of a potential security issue as its founder said the incident "does look like a hack on Binance." The company said late Thursday the estimated total impact was at more than $6 billion, which could be one of the most significant of such security incidents on record.

Business Crypto soared in 2025 — and then crashed. Now what? It wasn't immediately clear the extent of the damage hackers might have been able to cause, and Binance had not explicitly confirmed that funds had been pilfered. The company said its teams are "working around the clock" to resolve the issue.

"Rest assured that user funds are completely safe," a Binance spokesperson said in a statement.

"Our security teams are reviewing all relevant information with urgency, and we will provide updates through official Binance channels as soon as we have verified information," the statement continued.

The company wrote on its X account that the estimated total impact sat at around $6.3 billion. It said it has worked with blockchain partners to freeze affected assets, with roughly $3 billion frozen on-chain so far.

"Binance's initial investigation suggests that the security incident may involve a compromised DevOps engineer's laptop, which allowed an attacker to gain access to a service container and submit unauthorized withdrawal transactions," the company wrote.

"We have found no evidence of any wallet private key leak," it added.

national.summary: Assassins killed Carlos Manzo in the city of Uruapan last November during Day of the Dead celebrations, in a case that ignited fury across Mexico.
national.body: Mexican authorities arrested an official allegedly linked to the killing of a mayor who was vocal about drug violence, prosecutors reported on Thursday. Assassins killed Carlos Manzo in the city of Uruapan last November during Day of the Dead celebrations, in a case that ignited fury across Mexico last year. Uruapan's welfare secretary Rosa Alejandra Vargas was arrested "for her probable responsibility in the crime of concealment," Michoacan state prosecutors said in a statement. Vargas is related to several people already arrested in the case and had failed to appear when summoned by investigators, state prosecutor Israel Vega said.Manzo, 40, had gained popularity as a crusader against organized crime in the troubled state, and his death triggered huge anti-government protests. Investigations indicate the powerful Jalisco New Generation Cartel (CJNG) had ordered the attack on Manzo. Authorities have so far arrested 34 people over the killing. Deadly pattern of violenceManzo was among at least 13 mayors killed across Mexico in the two years since Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum took office, according to an Associated Press tally based on official reports. That compares with 23 sitting mayors killed during the previous administration's six years in office, according to civil society groups. The killings present a challenge for Sheinbaum as the Trump administration presses her government to crack down on cartels and root out corruption in local governments. Political violence has long been part of Mexico's cartel conflict, but it rarely touches the highest ranks of government. Cartels instead target local leaders, either corrupting them or killing those who stand in their way. Such killings often silence voices that threaten or interfere with cartel profits, said Miguel Meza, a researcher at the investigative organization Narcopoliticos.Last year, Bernardo Bravo, a leader of lime growers in Michoacan, was killed after repeatedly denouncing the extortion demands of organized crime on producers.In Uruapan, 250 miles west of Mexico City, Manzo's killing has sowed fear and uncertainty within his grassroots opposition Sombrero Movement, where he's gone from leader to martyr. national.body: When the journey of the MV Odyssey luxury cruise ship came to a sudden end earlier this week in Cambodia, giving residents on the ship just hours to disembark, it marked the culmination of several attempts over a period of about three months to save the unique voyage. national.title: The two most interesting risks to Anthropic
national.summary: Anthropic gave a 94-page list of risk factors in its S-1 this week. Two of them stood out.
national.body:
A TILE GAME is giving a boost to Chinese factories. Our very own Jennifer Pak reported that Chinese manufacturers have not had the easiest few years with U.S. tariffs and the war in Iran pushing up costs. Well, the aged game of Mahjong is giving them a surprising boost. That's because it's having a moment in the U.S. and some entrepreneurial citizens in China are enjoying the benefits. Mahjong sets can sell for like $300-$400 in the States … and want to know how much they cost to make? ~$30. One businessman said he used to make the game primarily for Chinese consumers. Now, every set is exported to the U.S.

What to Know: Anthropic gave the world 94 pages of risks to its business (slash the entire AI economy) in its IPO prospectus aka the S-1. It wouldn't be Anthropic if they didn't discuss the "existential risks" to humanity and society several times. And isn't that an important risk to disclose? Another that stood out: the AI boom has a glaring point of failure. The majority of advanced semiconductor manufacturing is concentrated in one place, Taiwan, and if anything were to happen there, it could disrupt the entire AI economy. Think earthquake, Chinese military action, blockades. But I want to focus on a different risk, because it is FASCINATING!

Committing to the past at a premium: Anthropic is worried about aging out of the tech that's powering its AI, while paying the same prices. What does that mean?! AI companies have to lock into pricey contracts for all sorts of softwares, hardware, data center, and squadrons of GPUs. But technology is advancing quickly right now. New GPUs, for example, could come along that can do the same amount of work for way less money. Then Anthropic is stuck like CHUMPS in a contract paying a premium for old hardware, while some competitors may be doing more for less.

What To Know: Microsoft offered buyouts to 60,000 employees, roughly a quarter of its staff this week. And doesn't that sound better than "Microsoft laid off 60,000 employees this week"?? Skydance ALSO offered a buyout to employees on Monday, though it's not clear how many would be eligible. And here at NPR, we've been a fan of the term buyout too. So what's the real difference in offering a buyout versus just laying off staffers?

The difference: Morale? Morale. There's something about a "mega-layoff" that doesn't inspire worker confidence. A "buyout" not so much. Really? Ok, I guess. The WSJ reported the focus in C-suite land is on the ratio of employees to AI agents inside companies. Companies have to find ways to pay for the ever-increasing costs of AI … and you know … actual human workers expect to be paid.

national.title: Helicopter carrying six people crashes in northern Indian state
national.summary: The aircraft reportedly took off from the Hindu pilgrimage site of Badrinath on Friday afternoon before losing contact.
national.body:
A search for survivors is under way after a helicopter carrying six people, including five pilgrims, crashed in the northern Indian state of Uttarakhand, officials say.

Uttarakhand's Chief Minister Pushkar Singh Dhami said the helicopter had crashed near a village close to Joshimath in Chamoli district. Rescue teams have been dispatched to the mountainous area, but the condition of those on board remains unclear.

The aircraft reportedly took off from the Hindu pilgrimage site of Badrinath on Friday afternoon before losing contact.

The cause of the crash is also not yet known. The incident happened amid reports of heavy rain and poor visibility in the region.

Uttarakhand, a Himalayan state which borders China and Nepal, is home to some of Hinduism's holiest shrines and attracts millions of pilgrims every year.

Badrinath is one of four sacred sites on the Char Dham pilgrimage circuit, alongside Kedarnath, Gangotri and Yamunotri. Many devotees travel through steep Himalayan valleys to reach the temples, which are open for only part of the year because of harsh winter conditions.

Helicopter services have become increasingly popular among pilgrims seeking to avoid difficult mountain journeys, but their safety has come under scrutiny following a series of accidents.

Friday's incident happened amid heavy rain in the region. India's weather department had issued an orange alert for the area, warning of thunderstorms, hail and strong winds.

national.summary: Christa Pike's failed execution in September, the state's second this year, has raised fresh questions about Tennessee's lethal injection execution process.
national.body: Christa Pike's failed execution in September has raised fresh questions about Tennessee's lethal injection execution protocol, which is in its fourth iteration in the past two decades. Pike's was the second botched execution by Tennessee this year. She had been sentenced to death for her role in the 1995 torture and murder of her 19-year-old classmate, Colleen Slemmer.CBS News reviewed the state's lethal injection protocols going back to 2007 and found that over the years the protocols grew increasingly vague. Kit Thomas, the deputy chief of the capital habeas unit at the Federal Public Defender's Office in Nashville and a critic of the state's current protocols, told CBS News that the protocol has been reduced "both in length and in details." Thomas said she is most familiar with the protocols since 2018.Prior to 2025, the Tennessee lethal injection protocols were laid out in detail over 100 pages and included extensive protocols about the various execution teams, their roles and responsibilities, the drugs used, established practices around IV lines and administering the lethal drugs. But in the most recent version, released to the public early last year, there were only 44 pages to guide members of the execution team through the process. Thomas believes that the state's move to a shorter protocol has shielded officials from accountability if something went awry. "When there are fewer rules, there are just fewer ways for you to be penalized," she told CBS News. Some of the most significant changes made were to the protocols governing the intravenous team, including how that team should place catheters and what to do if they faced difficulties administering the drugs. Thomas said those steps are some of the most consequential to carrying out a lethal injection. national.title: Campaign texts, powered by AI: How new tech is shaping voter outreach
national.summary: Campaigns are experimenting with AI texting to hear from more voters than before — and sometimes, to persuade them.
national.body: Washington — Ace Parsi describes himself as "personally pretty against AI." The Democrat is running an uphill race against Republican Rep. Riley Moore in ruby-red West Virginia and has drafted a legislative proposal to block new data centers that don't have buy-in from constituents.But after what he said was probably the most complicated decision of his campaign, Parsi and his team are using AI chatbots to text voters ahead of November's election."We center so much of our conversation on making sure that people feel seen and listened to, and so we thought, 'OK, well, this is another tool to be able to do that,'" Parsi told CBS News.Parsi's is one of a growing number of campaigns that are experimenting this midterm cycle with a new kind of voter canvassing: AI-powered text conversations that let campaigns talk with far more voters than staff and volunteers can reach on the ground. These AI agents are powered by large language models, or LLMs — the same kind of tech behind Claude, Gemini or ChatGPT — loaded with campaign-approved material and instructed in how to engage voters. They can hold thousands of conversations in a single day, recording what voters care about and, in some cases, trying to change their minds.Early research suggests the approach can work. One recent study in the journal Nature found that short conversations with AI chatbots in controlled experiments shifted voters' views more than political ads typically do.But the technology is moving faster than the rules around it. Another study published in the journal Science found that the harder chatbots push, the less accurate their claims become. Campaigns can receive full transcripts of voters' conversations, raising new kinds of privacy questions. national.title: Websites pretending to be local news are boosting Democratic candidates
national.summary: The websites of unknown origin are targeting key U.S. House races. They are getting picked up by ChatGPT's responses but Google's products avoid promoting them.
national.body:
Ahead of the midterms, some voters are turning to ChatGPT to help them decide who to vote for. When asked for information about candidates in some highly competitive races, NPR found that OpenAI's AI chatbot cited a set of websites that are thinly veiled political ads made to look like reporting from local news outlets.

Less than two weeks before Election Day, when asked "Which House candidates in [Michigan's 4th Congressional District] care about affordability?," the chatbot said Democrat Sean McCann had the "Most detailed published affordability plan" at the very top of its answer. The stakes in this race are high – it's one of the competitive U.S. House races that could determine control of the chamber.

ChatGPT's response when NPR asked "Which House candidates in [Michigan's 4th Congressional District] care about affordability?" hide caption

As a citation, ChatGPT linked to a website called the Kalamazoo Beacon. The Beacon labels its articles as "news articles" in the website's source code. The outlet also describes itself in the site's source code as "Reporting on Kalamazoo, southwest Michigan, and the issues shaping lakeshore communities."

But the Kalamazoo Beacon has only published 16 stories, all about McCann, his policy positions and his record as a state legislator, NPR's review shows.

The Beacon is one of 10 "local news" websites that promote one Democrat apiece in competitive U.S. House races. The 10 sites are part of a larger group of 37 websites identified by the digital security firm VisionHeight that promote many more candidates, mostly Democrats, for a slew of federal, state and local offices, as well as some nonpartisan posts like judges.

While it makes sense that political campaigns and their allies would try to optimize their message for pickup by AI chatbots, pretending to operate as news outlets crosses a line into deception, said Renée DiResta, an associate research professor at Georgetown University who studies online influence campaigns.

When users ask AI chatbots questions, less-credible websites can make an appearance when the chatbots search the internet and summarize the content of links in the search results.

national.title: For voters from immigrant families and new citizens, voting is bigger than themselves
national.summary: While many young voters are focused on the cost of living in the election, for some from immigrant families, the political calculation — and their votes — is often about even more than the economy.
national.body:
Nicole Solis-Sison on the day she became a naturalized citizen. Solis-Sison first came to the U.S. from the Philippines when she was 7. Courtesy of Nicole Solis-Sison hide caption

Nicole Solis-Sison moved to America when she was seven years old. Her parents and immediate family were fleeing the Philippine government and sought asylum in the U.S.

When they landed in Los Angeles, Solis-Sison thought their stay would be temporary. Eventually, once things calmed down in her home country, they would return. That wasn't the case.

"The Philippine government pursued us in international immigration territory and demanded that we be sent back," she told NPR.

That's when an agent with the then-Immigration and Naturalization Services agency — which has since been renamed Immigration and Customs Enforcement, or ICE — showed up to her house. They were prepared to be deported. But after the agent interviewed her family, they weren't packing their bags back to Manila.

"This particular INS [Immigration and Naturalization Services] agent suggested that we should file for asylum, given that we were on U.S. soil," Solis-Sison said.

An immigration agent, Solis-Sison said, gave her family the tools needed to stay in the U.S. legally. Earlier this year, after more than two decades navigating the immigration system, she became an American citizen. Now, at the age of 34, Solis-Sison is voting in her very first election in New York City.

"This is like such a milestone year for me that I'm a first time voter. I created my own voter guide and voter diary," she said.

Consider: Musk has donated more $400 million dollars to Republican causes ahead of this year's midterm elections — far more than mega-donors Michael Bloomberg and George Soros have given to Democrats combined, according to media outlets including The Washington Post and CNN.

This month, Musk's company SpaceX temporarily restricted Ukraine's use of the Starlink satellite system, causing some Ukrainian drones to fall from the sky.

Over the years, Musk's companies, including SpaceX and Tesla, have received more than $30 billion in federal contracts, subsidies, loans and tax credits.

"I call it an unholy alliance," says Nasaw. "He makes money and then he returns that money to keep those who are friendly to him in power."

Most of the U.S. will "fall back" an hour when the clocks change at 2 a.m. on the first Sunday of November.Here's what to know about what's formally known as daylight saving time as it ends for the year:What is daylight saving time, and why do we have it?Daylight saving time is the period during the year, from March to early November, when the majority of the U.S. operates one hour ahead of standard time.The move effectively "saves" an hour of daylight from the morning and adds it to the evening during the spring and summer months when the days are the longest. In the fall and winter months, when the days are shorter, the U.S. returns to standard time, with daylight coming earlier in the morning.For example, in Boston on Saturday, before the time change, the sun will rise at 7:16 a.m. and set at 5:39 p.m., according to the National Weather Service. On Sunday, back on standard time, sunrise will be at 6:17 a.m. and sunset will be at 4:37 p.m.The U.S. first adopted daylight saving time in 1918 during World War I as an effort to conserve fuel after Europe implemented its own time change, according to the Congressional Research Service. After the war, Congress repealed the clock switch but gave states the option to continue observing it.During World War II and the 1970s energy crisis, Congress brought year-round daylight saving time to the U.S., again with the goal of reducing energy consumption. These experiments didn't last long.After the war, the U.S. let states and municipalities decide for themselves if they wanted to keep daylight saving time and when to observe it. (Congress didn't establish a uniform start and end for the time change until 1966.) In the '70s, continuous daylight saving time was stopped before reaching the 10-month mark.Will the U.S. move to year-round daylight saving time?Earlier this year, legislation to once again make daylight saving time last all year long cleared a major hurdle in Congress. Sir Patrick Stewart: The life of an iconic actor Close Iconic Star Trek actor Sir Patrick Stewart has died aged 86.

Sir Patrick died at his home in Los Angeles on 28 October after "a brief and poignant journey" with Alzheimer's disease and Lewy Body Dementia, according to a statement shared on his social media.

“His sonorous voice and singular talent will forever be synonymous with indelible performances in every genre,” the statement reads.

In a career that spanned seven decades, Sir Patrick won multiple Emmys and Golden Globes, a star on the Hollywood Walk of Fame and a knighthood from Queen Elizabeth II.

local.title: New York state comptroller candidates offer differing outlooks
local.summary: State Comptroller Thomas DiNapoli is facing a challenge from New York City businessman Joseph Hernandez in his bid for re-election.
local.body:
State Comptroller Thomas DiNapoli , currently the longest-serving statewide official, is making the argument that experience counts as the Democrat seeks re-election.

But his Republican opponent, New York City businessman Joseph Hernandez , says DiNapoli hasn’t done enough to combat fraud and abuse in state government during his 19 years in office. And that the state pension fund is underperforming.

The comptroller oversees the fund and serves a watchdog function over the spending of state and local tax dollars.

“When you look at the performance of the S&P, for example, last quarter the S&P generated about 15% return,” Hernandez said during their only debate, which was televised by Spectrum News NY1. "Nasdaq generated 21%. So when you say you did well at 6.2%, that's not the full score.”

“I've tried very hard to de-risk the fund as best as possible to provide that retirement security,” DiNapoli said during the debate. “We have an assumed rate of return of 5.9%, one of the lowest in the country. It means we don't have to take risky bets because there are market cycles.”

DiNapoli first took office in 2007, elected by the Legislature after the resignation of then-Comptroller Alan Hevesi. DiNapoli said he’s prided himself on cleaning up the office and rooting out fraud in state government.

“I want to continue our audits and our investigations to make government more cost-effective, reduce costs to our taxpayers, and hold wrongdoers accountable,” he said.

He highlighted the office’s work on Medicaid, citing 55 arrests and $44 million in recovered funds since 2023.

local.summary: The Brighton Central School District is again moving forward with plans to build an athletic field behind its high school. But first, soil and air in the area are being tested for contamination.
local.body:
Listen • 1:18 The Brighton Central School District is again moving forward with plans to build an athletic field behind its high school. But first, soil and air in the area are being tested for contamination.

The district put the turf field project on pause in March after soil contamination was discovered by a contractor. Now, it's moving forward with a cleanup so it can resume construction of the field behind the high school.

The cost of that work is about $3 million according to an Interim Site Management Plan published in May.

According to that document, an alternative approach to remove all contamination, or "historic fill materials," would amount to more than 15 million dollars. Fill materials in this case refer to cinder, ash, glass, brick, metal and ceramics buried up to seven feet below the surface. Mercury and cyanide were also detected in soil samples taken earlier this year.

The district has scheduled a community forum at 7 p.m. Nov. 17 at the Administrative Building, 2035 Monroe Ave. State Department of Environmental Conservation representatives and the district's environmental consultants are expected to attend to answer residents’ questions.

local.body:
No one needs to explain to New York gubernatorial candidate Bruce Blakeman that he and his team need to run hard through the tape on Election Day. They're doing that.

Hence the Oct. 28 whistle-stop tour across the Southern Tier from Owego to Elmira to Hornell to Olean to Lakewood.

Not every candidate can be passionate without being--or at least coming off as--angry.

It would be rare for a red candidate to be the favorite in a statewide election in a dark blue state such as New York, especially when the president is a Republican, no matter who the president is.

Everyone should know Blakeman isn't the favorite. Yet under the circumstances--principally an unpopular incumbent and a state that's in trouble--Blakeman can win.

If those who are with him on issues vote for him in a big turnout.

New York has 62 counties. Blakeman will win more than 50. To prevail statewide, however, he needs to win them overwhelmingly with a big turnout.

Just to pick an extreme example, it won't cut it for him to win Chautauqua County with a low turnout and a percentage of the vote in the low 50s.

local.body:
Judy was the embodiment of love and kindness. In every role she held, she truly searched for a way to make the day a little brighter, or to make life a little less heavy for everyone she encountered- always putting the needs of others before her own. Her warm smile, sense of humor, and loving heart carried her through her final years as she relished reminiscing with schoolmates, friends, caregivers and family.

As a young woman, Judy enjoyed attending the Westfield Presbyterian Church as a member of the choir, and was active in the Columbine Crown Chapter of the Order of the Eastern Star where she was the flag bearer. Additionally, Judy was a gifted knitter and spent many years bowling in the Barcelona Lanes League where she was recognized for high game and high series achievements.

Judy entered the work force in 1959 following graduation from Westfield Academy and Central School, beginning a lengthy career as a Dental Assistant in the Jamestown and Westfield areas with Drs. Carstensen, Johnson, Militello and Scholl. She married her husband of 42 years, the late Richard Haynes, in 1966 and they welcomed their first daughter Melinda a year later, followed by Elizabeth in 1970, and Suzanne in 1971. Her family was her entire world, and she worked tirelessly to provide a loving home.

Later, Judy's career journey brought her to the Brocton Central School district, Johnson's Adult Home as a care giver and finally as a wellness leader at the WCA Home in Fredonia, NY where she led the ladies through crafting activities, chair yoga and cultural outings at Fredonia State College. Valuing each client as though they were family, Judy stated that she cared for them the same way she hoped to be honored when she became their age. As the cafeteria MOM-iter at Brocton Central, Judy cherished each student as she would her own child, complete with chin wiping and spill management. She loved the extra opportunity to see her kids and friends in the middle of the day, always ready with a smile and a warm hug for anyone who needed it. Those were some of her favorite years, and she always spoke fondly of the many youngsters who created a memory and left an imprint upon her heart. You all know who you are, and we thank you.

Judy is survived by her daughters, Elizabeth and Suzanne, her siblings, Elaine, Merillee, Leslie, Bill and Jon, sister-in-law, Anita, brother-in-law, Orlin, numerous Grand and Great-grandchildren, nieces and nephews, all of whom she loved so dearly. She is pre-deceased by her daughter, Melinda, husband, Richard, brother, Robert, sisters-in law, Florence and Jean, mother, Margaret Burlingame Miller and father, Howard M. Jones.

local.body:
MILWAUKEE (AP) -- Milwaukee could come to a standstill as fans celebrate the Brewers’ first World Series title.

Thousands of fans are expected to line the streets for a victory parade on Friday, forcing the state’s largest school district in Milwaukee to close because of operational and safety concerns.

The small-market Brewers gave their long-suffering fans the title they had been waiting for with a 4-1 win over the Tampa Bay Rays on Wednesday, clinching the series in five games.

Thousands of Brewers fans filled the Trop -- nearly outnumbering Rays’ fans -- and celebrated from the stands after the final out. Thousands more celebrated back in Milwaukee, where the party will continue with Friday’s parade.

Milwaukee Public Schools canceled classes on Friday, allowing fans to enjoy the parade that will run through downtown and conclude with a fan fest at Henry Maier Festival Park, not far from the shore of Lake Michigan.

Michael Maxwell, the presiding judge in neighboring Waukesha County, declared Brewers attire will be formally considered “in compliance with professional decorum expected of courtroom staff, litigants and attorneys appearing before the court” through the conclusion of the victory parade.

One fan who joined the queue to get tickets for the rally at American Family Insurance Amphitheater said he was behind 34,000 people -- at 8 a.m.

A large police presence is expected for the parade to handle the big crowds and heavy traffic.

local.summary: Chuck Nazzaro is once again a member of the Chautauqua County Legislature – though for how long is open to debate. Nazzaro took his oath of office to fill the unexpired term of Vince DeJoy, who resigned earlier this month after moving to North Carolina. Nazzaro’s appointment is through Dec. 31. Nazz
local.body:
Chuck Nazzaro is once again a member of the Chautauqua County Legislature – though for how long is open to debate.

Nazzaro took his oath of office to fill the unexpired term of Vince DeJoy, who resigned earlier this month after moving to North Carolina. Nazzaro's appointment is through Dec. 31. Nazzaro served on the Chautauqua County Legislature for 14 years, finishing his last term in 2022. Nazzaro was first elected to the county legislature in 2008 and served for 14 years. He was a Jamestown city council member before his election to the legislature. Nazzaro chaired the legislature's Audit and Control Committee when either the Democrats or the Republicans controlled the body.

DeJoy's name remains on the ballot, and should DeJoy receive the most votes in Tuesday's election Nazzaro would need to be appointed again in January.

And, with Election Day less than a week away, there is a war of words between the county Republican and Democratic parties over what a vote for DeJoy would mean.

The Chautauqua County Democratic Committee, working with the Jamestown Democratic Committee, has asked Nazzaro to fill the remainder of DeJoy's term this year and commit to serving through at least 2027 when a special election will be held.

"We were surprised by Vince DeJoy's announcement. We are excited to have a well-respected public servant and civic-minded person such as Chuck Nazzaro to stand in if DeJoy receives the winning number of votes," said Marcia Westling-Johnson, county Democratic Party chair. "It is a short time to voting. We are optimistic that District 9 residents will vote for DeJoy on the ballot knowing that they will be getting Nazzaro as their legislator."

Republicans, in their own news release, said the issue isn't that cut and dried. While Nazzaro has said he will serve in 2027 until a special election is held, there is no requirement that he be the party's appointed choice.

"But what happens after January 1? There is no guarantee that Nazzaro will remain in the seat, leaving voters at the mercy of party insiders and backroom political decisions," the county Republican Party said in a news release.

local.title: Another impeachment is a mixed result
local.summary: A coalition of right-wing organizations and activists is lobbying the White House to grant mass pardons to junior staffers in the administration. “A pardon for all junior administration personnel is viewed as unlikely,” one source told the Washington Sun, “but the president could issue blanket pardo
local.body:
A coalition of right-wing organizations and activists is lobbying the White House to grant mass pardons to junior staffers in the administration. “A pardon for all junior administration personnel is viewed as unlikely,” one source told the Washington Sun, “but the president could issue blanket pardons for all employees involved in particular policy areas, such as deportations, war or trade.”

There’s a raging debate within the Democratic Party, mostly beneath the surface, about whether President Trump should be impeached for a third time. It’s relevant because the Democrats are almost guaranteed to win back the House, and therefore the power to impeach.

But the debate isn’t over whether Trump has done anything impeachable. That question is settled: Of course he has. Democrats are debating whether it would be politically wise to stir up all the drama only to inevitably fail at securing the two-thirds vote requirement for conviction in the Senate. Spending the next two years on a failed impeachment wouldn’t fulfill their promises to deal with “affordability” and the like.

I don’t really care about the politics one way or another. But if Democrats decide to go down that path, Trump’s abuse of the pardon power would be a good place to start.

There’s ample evidence that various figures have outright bought pardons, or received them in trade for political services rendered. If you don’t think that’s impeachable, take it up with James Madison, who insisted that a president handing out pardons in exchange for nefarious activity done on his behalf would be impeachable. You know, like sitting back as the Capitol is ransacked after your efforts to steal an election fail. Then again, Trump was already impeached for that, and the Senate refused to convict him.

And that’s the problem. Hyperpartisanship has nullified the impeachment power. If Jan. 6 wasn’t enough, what’s the point of trying again?

There are only two relevant replies to that question: If impeachment is in the political interests of the opposition party, and if it’s the right thing to do whether or not it’s in their interest.

I can come up with several more candidates for reasons to impeach Trump because it’s the right thing to do. Whether it would be in the political interest of the Democrats is a much tougher question to answer. It depends in part on the specific abuses and on the evidence. But it’s not obvious to me that any evidence would be compelling enough to get roughly half the GOP Senate caucus to convict, and that’s assuming the Senate would even take up the impeachment in the first place. That would depend on whether Democrats take the Senate.

local.title: Allen looks to renew rivalry with Jackson
local.summary: ORCHARD PARK — Josh Allen can appreciate how heated discussions can get over bar stools, on talk radio and social media over whether he or Lamar Jackson are the better quarterback. It’s a debate that has raged since the two were selected in the first round of the 2018 draft. Just don’t ask him to […
local.body:
ORCHARD PARK -- Josh Allen can appreciate how heated discussions can get over bar stools, on talk radio and social media over whether he or Lamar Jackson are the better quarterback.

It’s a debate that has raged since the two were selected in the first round of the 2018 draft. Just don’t ask him to take sides, even as Allen has an opportunity to move the needle Sunday when the AFC East-leading Buffalo Bills (5-1) host Baltimore Ravens (4-3).

“He’s been one of the best if not the best quarterback. And what he’s consistently done when he’s on the field is unbelievable,” Allen said of Jackson. “He’s a very special player and I’ve got so much respect for him.

“That’s why you play this game is to have matchups like this.”

Though the quarterbacks are 2-2 in head-to-head regular-season meetings, Allen is 2-0 in the playoffs. Jackson, meantime, has the edge in being a two-time NFL MVP versus Allen winning the honor once.

Refreshed from a bye week off, Allen is expected to be on the field Sunday. The question is Jackson’s status, as the quarterback resumed practicing after missing the past three outings with an ankle injury.

The Ravens can certainly use a boost after losing two straight, including a 35-13 loss to Cincinnati in which Baltimore squandered a 13-0 halftime lead.

“We have to pick each other up to move on to the next one and get that one, because we need a jumpstart,” wide receiver Zay Flowers said before noting that spark could come in the form of Jackson back behind center.

local.body:
SINCLAIRVILLE -- No. 1 Cassadaga Valley kicked off its run in the Section VI Class D volleyball playoffs with a sweep against No. 8 Sherman 26-24, 25-22, 25-20 on Thursday evening.

"I'm incredibly proud of our girls tonight," Cassadaga Valley head coach Melissa Kelly said about the win. "We knew Sherman was going to be a tough opponent, and they certainly proved that. Cassadaga Valley (16-3) was led by Kailee Lacki with 12 kills, five digs and five points, Melanie Myles made 30 assists, seven digs and 12 points, Aleix Pattyson provided nine kills, Anna Burlingame had seven kills and a block and Eliana Katilus added 13 digs, two aces and seven points.

"Burlingame had an outstanding game and really rose to the occasion, while fellow senior Melanie Myles was huge for us on the serving line. Those are the kinds of contributions you need in a postseason match. Our girls had to work for every point, stay composed, and trust one another, and I'm proud of how they responded. This is what playoff volleyball is all about, and we're excited to have the opportunity to keep playing."

Emmersen Crawford led the Sherman (6-13) effort with eight kills, Madison Emory had three aces and three kills, Jayne Chambers provided four kills and three blocks and Ava Irwin dealt 15 assists.

local.summary: The site of a vacant police precinct in Buffalo's Old First Ward will now become the city's brand-new animal shelter.
local.body: The site of a vacant police precinct in Buffalo's Old First Ward will now become the city's brand-new animal shelter.The parcel at 294 Louisiana Street was once used to train police canines. In a nod to its past, it will now house Buffalo's four-legged friends in its new lease of life as the city's animal shelter. Though the final design process has yet to take place, Buffalo Mayor Sean Ryan said the shelter will be a revamp of its existing structure, four times bigger than the current facility on Oak Street. The shelter will have capacity to house around 100 dogs and between 90 and 130 cats, according to the mayor's office. The former shelter was designed to hold 66 dogs and 59 cats and is often over capacity, with a 2024 7 News I-Team investigation revealing the poor conditions at the facility. WATCH: 'Borderline abandoned': Conditions, care of animals called to question at City of Buffalo animal shelterThe Louisiana Street site was selected with help from a committee of Buffalo Animal Shelter volunteers. "Today marks a milestone decades in the making," said Kelly Gorman, who is on the committee. "Cats will be able to see daylight from their kennels and stretch their legs in community cat rooms. Dogs will have opportunity for exercise in multiple large play-yards." The new facility will be a $30 million capital project, with the site chosen for its access to the nearby green space of Father Conway Park and transportation links.But could there be trouble ahead in getting funding for this project? The mayor needs to request to borrow money to get the project going through the city's capital budget, and that's not exactly been a smooth ride over the past few years."Every project in the City of Buffalo has been delayed because of the borrowing fight with the comptroller," Ryan explained.Borrowing signed off by the common council to fund projects such as road repaving and community center repairs has been on hold after the city comptroller, Barbara Miller-Williams, questioned the amount the city wanted to borrow. local.title: South Buffalo neighbors divided over future of historic Eden Street brick road
local.summary: A plan to pave a nearly century-old brick street in South Buffalo is on hold after neighbors raised concerns about preserving the roadway.
local.body: A plan to pave a nearly century-old brick street in South Buffalo is on hold after neighbors raised concerns about preserving the roadway.On Eden Street, some neighbors think the red brick is an attractive part of the neighborhood, but it has deteriorated."I do love the brick, but I think it's time for it to go," Molly Griffin said. Griffin and her mother, Janie Griffin, live on Eden near Abbott Road, where they said the condition of the street is particularly rough."There's bumps all over the place," Janie Griffin said. "When the snowplows come down, you can just hear it grind. My car is constantly bumping."Jim Skrzeczkowski, who grew up on Eden Street and whose mother and sister still live there, also favors paving the street."I've always thought it should be paved over," Skrzeczkowski said. "Aesthetically, it's really nice to look at and everything, but if you're here in the wintertime and you're trying to get around, and for plowing reasons and everything, it's very difficult."Other residents want to preserve Eden Street's distinctive brick.Leonidas Longworth said he would prefer Buffalo invest in restoring historic features rather than covering or replacing them."I'd rather honestly invest in restoring the historic parts of Buffalo and bringing them back to what they used to look like, rather than tearing it all up and replacing it with something easier or cheaper," Longworth said.Some neighbors signed a petition to pave over the roadway, while others signed a petition calling for the brick to be preserved.Preservation Buffalo Niagara has since applied to have Eden Street designated as a City of Buffalo landmark, noting that the vitrified brick roadway was installed in 1928.The paving project is now paused, although crews were on Eden Street Thursday working on driveway aprons.Common Councilmember Chris Scanlon said the city wants to hear from residents before deciding what happens next."So it has been paused," Scanlon said. "Obviously, this is a public project. This is a public works project. And we want public input on it."WATCH: South Buffalo neighbors divided over future of historic Eden Street brick roadwayThe Department of Public Works is scheduled to hold a community meeting Monday at 5:30 p.m. at the Tosh Collins Community Center. local.title: Fewer Monroe County children had elevated levels of lead in their blood in 2025
local.summary: Also, more children in Monroe County were tested for lead in their blood in 2025 than in the previous year.
local.body:
More children in Monroe County were tested for lead in their blood in 2025, but the number of them found to have elevated levels fell by 27%, according to data released Thursday by the county.

In total, 14,556 children were tested, and of them, 217 exceeded the county's threshold of 5 micrograms per deciliter. That's compared to 299 in 2024.

The federal Centers for Disease Control and Prevention considers blood lead levels in children to be elevated if they exceed 3.5 micrograms per deciliter. The consensus among health experts is that there is no known level of lead in children's blood that is safe.

When children in Monroe County are found to have elevated blood lead levels, the Department of Public Health intervenes. Its Lead Poisoning Prevention program provides follow-up care, including medical case management and educational outreach. Staff also investigate the children's homes to identify sources of lead exposure.

entertainment.title: Edinburgh Film Festival Toasts Bollywood With ‘Kuch Kuch Hota Hai’ Anniversary Event at 2028 Edition
entertainment.summary: Superstars of Indian cinema Shah Rukh Khan and Kajol lead Karan Johar's cult favorite.
entertainment.body:
Bollywood is coming to the Edinburgh International Film Festival .

EIFF on Friday confirmed that a special 30th anniversary celebration of the legendary Indian film Kuch Kuch Hota Hai (1998) will screen as part of the 2028 edition.

Partly filmed in Scotland, the beloved cult favorite — and Karan Johar’s directorial debut, following the love triangle between Rahul Khanna ( Shah Rukh Khan ), Anjali Sharma ( Kajol ) and Tina Malhotra (Rani Mukerji) — will return to the cinema to celebrate its enduring legacy as a landmark of Indian cinema, with Johar and other guests in attendance. Related Stories Movies From 'Sh*t Happens' to an Erotic Photographer Being Confronted by His Daughter: Offbeat Films at Tallinn Movies Jamie Dornan Boards 'Nostalgie,' Starring Aidan Gillen as Washed-up Pop Star, as Executive Producer (Exclusive)

Johar was invited to mark Kuch Kuch Hota Hai ‘s anniversary at the 2028 EIFF during a meeting he hosted in the Mumbai offices of his production company, Dharma Productions, earlier this week with the First Minister of Scotland, John Swinney, and Screen Scotland’s interim executive director, David Smith.

The meeting, said EIFF, was focused on Scotland’s potential as a destination and partner for Indian film and television production, co-production, talent development and cultural exchange. Kuch Kuch Hota Hai was the first major Indian production to film extensively across Scotland, including Eilean Donan Castle, Glen Coe, Tantallon Castle and Inchmahome Priory.

Swinney said: “It was a pleasure to meet Karan Johar in Mumbai […] I look forward to welcoming him to Edinburgh. During my visit to India, I met with people from the Indian film industry, including representatives from Dharma Productions, to discuss opportunities for future collaboration between Scottish and Indian filmmaking. Scotland’s screen industry has tremendous potential as a creative partner for Indian film and television, offering the infrastructure, expertise and world-class filming locations to support a wide range of productions.”

EIFF CEO and festival director Paul Ridd said his team is always thinking about the future and what’s next. “So we jumped at an opportunity like this,” he said, “to plant the seeds for a celebration of a legendary, much-loved film at our festival, a film featuring Scotland and some of the most iconic stars of Bollywood cinema on screen. We can’t wait for what promises to be something truly special for our 81st edition in 2028. But in the meantime, watch this space for more news of our 80th next August.”

entertainment.title: Foo Fighters Close Out ‘Kimmel’ Residency With ‘Baker Street’ Cover: Watch
entertainment.summary: A guilty pleasure of Dave Grohl, “Baker Street” was the Foos' only cover this week on "Fallon."
entertainment.body:
Foo Fighters Week on Jimmy Kimmel Live came to a close in the small hours of Friday morning, with another oldie, but a goodie.

The choice of song, a cover of the late Gerry Rafferty ’s classic “Baker Street,” well, it was no secret. Foos frontman Dave Grohl told us what to expect earlier in the week, during his interview with Kimmel.

For Grohl, “Baker Street” is a proper guilty pleasure. “I don’t know if anyone remembers Gerry Rafferty. ‘Right Down The Line,’ ‘Baker Street’. He was in Stealers Wheel, ‘Stuck In The Middle With You.’ ‘Baker Street’ is one of my favorite songs of all time,” he recounted. “It reminds me of being young in the ‘70s. And driving around with my mom in the front seat, with AM radio on. It is truly one of my favorite songs of all time. We’ll rock that.” Related Selena Gomez Celebrates 'Ups & Downs' With Demi Lovato: 'I'm Proud of What We've Been Through' Meet Leah Barylsky, the Woman Behind the Camera - And On the Stage -- During Rüfüs Du Sol's Record-Breaking Tour Will My Chemical Romance Score Its First No. 1 Album Next Week (With a 20-Year-Old Album)? Explore Foo Fighters Gerry Rafferty See latest videos, charts and news

They sure did. The Foos, as they’ve done for the four consecutive nights, cranked the guitars, Grohl engaged in some gentle headbanging, and Ilan Rubin channeled Animal from behind the kit. No, the Foos didn’t augment their lineup with a synth of a saxophone player, instead lead guitarist Chris Shiflett interpreted that famous riff.

Rafferty, the Scottish-born singer and songwriter, enjoyed a global hit with “Baker Street,” which peaked at No. 2 on the Billboard Hot 100 in 1978, one of his six solo appearances on the chart. He died from liver failure in 2011, following a long battle with alcoholism.

“Baker Street” was the Foos’ only cover on Fallon this week , after performances of “Window” from the rock act’s 12th and latest studio album, Your Favorite Toy; 1995 ripper “This Is A Call,” from the band’s self-titled debut; and “Your Favorite Toy. ”

The Foos’ world tour has this year taken the Rock Hall-inductees through North America, across Europe, and next week gets underway in Australia .

entertainment.title: Jamie Dornan Boards ‘Nostalgie,’ Starring Aidan Gillen as Washed-up Pop Star, as Executive Producer (Exclusive)
entertainment.summary: Kathryn Ferguson’s IFTA-winning short film features original music by Bastille’s Dan Smith and cinematography by two-time Oscar nominee Robbie Ryan.
entertainment.body:
Jamie Dornan ( Belfast , The Tourist , Fifty Shades of Grey , The Fall ) has boarded director Kathryn Ferguson’s ( Nothing Compares ) IFTA-winning, BAFTA-nominated and Oscar-qualified short film Nostalgie as executive producer, throwing his support and star power behind the Northern Irish production as it heads into awards season, including a possible spot in the best live action short film Oscars race.

The darkly comic drama, which examines artistic ownership and the unpredictable relationship between musicians and their audiences, stars Aidan Gillen ( Game of Thrones , The Wire , Kin ) and features original songs and a score by BRIT Award-winning Bastille frontman Dan Smith , with cinematography by two-time Oscar nominee Robbie Ryan ( Poor Things , The Favourite ). Related Stories Movies 'Godzilla Minus Zero': First Reactions Lifestyle Japan's TeamLab Bringing Permanent Digital Art Exhibition Space to California

For the Belfast-born Dornan, joining the project represents an opportunity to champion filmmaking talent from his home city. “I’m always keeping my eyes and ears open for exciting productions being filmed back home,” he said. “So, when the opportunity arose to join Nostalgie as an executive producer, working alongside a largely Belfast-born team, it was an absolute no-brainer.”

And he lauded the director: “Kathryn has captured the raw, visceral tribalism that exists within the complex social and political landscape of Northern Ireland, while telling a story that feels deeply human, relatable and universal,” Dornan said. “Achieving that balance is no small feat, and it is a testament to her remarkable talent and vision as a storyteller.”

Adapted from a short story by Belfast author Wendy Erskine, Nostalgie follows Drew Lord Haig (Gillen), a washed-up 1980s pop star who is unexpectedly invited to perform at a centenary celebration in Belfast. “Hoping to relive his glory days, he discovers that one of his forgotten songs has become an unlikely anthem, taking on a meaning he could never have imagined,” notes a synopsis. “The film explores a dilemma familiar to musicians everywhere: What happens when a song takes on a life of its own, and its creator loses control over what it comes to represent?”

Written by Stacey Gregg ( Bad Sisters , Mary & George ), the film also stars Michael Smiley ( Bad Sisters ), Jessica Reynolds ( Kneecap ), Seamus O’Hara ( An Irish Goodbye, House of Guinness ) and Sean Kearns ( The Boxer ).

Related Selena Gomez Celebrates 'Ups & Downs' With Demi Lovato: 'I'm Proud of What We've Been Through' Meet Leah Barylsky, the Woman Behind the Camera - And On the Stage -- During Rüfüs Du Sol's Record-Breaking Tour Will My Chemical Romance Score Its First No. 1 Album Next Week (With a 20-Year-Old Album)?

This week, Dominic Fike drops his first LP as a minted hitmaker; Mariah Carey takes another glance at her polarizing Glitter project and Queens of the Stone Age turns down the amps for its ninth album… plus much more.

It feels like one of 2026’s most-anticipated LPs, given how this was the year that mainstream-adjacent singer-songwriter Dominic Fike belatedly proved himself as a pop hitmaker, with the long-running Hot 100 hits “Babydoll” and “White Keys.” But while How to Quit Smoking is one of the autumn’s most satisfying arrivals, its relatively lo-fi, genre-agnostic vibes show how unlikely Fike’s top 40 dalliances were in the first place — including with “White Keys,” present here as something of an album centerpiece — and how another such hit is far from required for the album to be deemable as a success. Its charms are mostly gentle and acoustic, but with at least a toe kept in hip-hop, leading to winningly unpredictable moments like the Danny Brown guest verse on “Not the Spirit,” an ODB interpolation on “Not the Spirit” and a thoroughly disarming Tay-K appearance (via phone) that closes the album.

As Cher Horowitz once said about report card grades, it appears that album releases are just a jumping-off point to start negotiations for Gracie Abrams. After scoring the biggest hit of her The Secret of Us era in 2024 with the deluxe edition cut “That’s So True,” it feels like she could be on track for a second straight bonus high-water mark with “Here You Come, There You Go,” lead track from her upcoming Daughter From Hell deluxe edition. entertainment.title: After an Incredible Brush With Dolly Parton, Fanny Lumsden Celebrates Her ‘Traditions’
entertainment.summary: Lumsden talks Dolly Parton, Paul Kelly and her new album, the followup to her ARIA Award winner "Hey Dawn."
entertainment.body:
Just three years ago, Fanny Lumsden had an on-stage moment that’s near-impossible to beat. When her last LP, Hey Dawn , collected the prize for best country album at the 2023 ARIA Awards , it was the late Queen of Country, Dolly Parton , who announced the winner . “Dolly Parton said my name,” Lumsden reminisced in a post on Substack , published in July of this year. “Not only was this the high point of my career so far but maybe one of my life.” Related Selena Gomez Celebrates 'Ups & Downs' With Demi Lovato: 'I'm Proud of What We've Been Through' Meet Leah Barylsky, the Woman Behind the Camera - And On the Stage -- During Rüfüs Du Sol's Record-Breaking Tour Will My Chemical Romance Score Its First No. 1 Album Next Week (With a 20-Year-Old Album)? Explore Dolly Parton Fanny Lumsden Paul Kelly See latest videos, charts and news

A high point, yes, but Lumsden has many more highlights to come.

Today (Oct. 30), the Australian singer, songwriter and bandleader invites us in for Traditions, her fifth studio album. On it, Lumsden explores the value and meaning that can come from our traditions, and how they shape us. Some ought to be reconciled or resolved. Others, perhaps, consigned to landfill.

Across its 11 songs, Fanny acknowledges the traditions of her upbringing, whilst also “staying true to my autonomy, and my ambition, and being a woman, and being progressive in all of that space,” she tells Billboard over a Zoom from her property in Tooma, on the western side of the Snowy Mountains, NSW. “I’m trying to figure out which ones I celebrate and which ones I have to change to keep. And then which ones we just chuck out altogether.”

Lumsden, like so many of us, had a spring cleaning with her family traditions. And like a growing number of descendants of white settlers, a reckoning with Australia’s modern history and an awareness of its flaws. “I decided they didn’t quite fit me properly, so I threw them all out,” she recounts. “And then I was like, oh no, that’s not how that works. You can change things, you can celebrate a little bit of it.”

Produced by Steven Schram (Crowded House, The Cat Empire, Paul Kelly), Traditions was recorded live over nine days with her band, The Daddies (also known as the Prawn Stars).

“I didn’t go in with a clear understanding of exactly what this theme was, although I did have the world and the vision. The colors and the visual. I knew I wanted to celebrate that world in some way,” she explains. It wasn’t until after the album was completed that Lumsden realized she could “see it through all the songs.”

entertainment.body:

Just when you thought American Horror Story couldn’t get any crazier, the FX horror anthology delivered its season 13 finale — bringing its battle between the Coven and Satan to a close.

Throughout the season, the witches have been doing everything in their power to defeat young Mr. Nas (aka Satan, played by Paul Anthony Kelly ). Following last week’s major revelations that Ben (Joey Pollari) is Satan’s son and that Constance Langdon and Fiona Goode (both played by Jessica Lange) are twin sisters and daughters of Satan and Sister Jude (also played by Lange), the stakes reach their highest point in Thursday’s finale. In the concluding episode, young Mr. Nas kills his medical specialist, Mr. Phibes (John Waters), as well as the older version of himself. Meanwhile, Fiona introduces Constance to the basics of witchcraft, hinting at her potential place within the Coven. Ben and Madison’s (Emma Roberts) romance also takes an unexpected turn when, immediately after the two have sex, Madison becomes pregnant and gives birth to their daughter. When the newborn appears to be dead, young Mr. Nas brings the baby back to life.

But the witches aren’t done fighting. After Mallory (Billie Lourd) travels through time once again, she and Cordelia (Sarah Paulson) realize what they must do to save the world: convince Ben to sacrifice himself. Ben ultimately agrees and stabs himself in the heart with a sword, turning to ashes and defeating Satan. Young Mr. Nas is left trapped inside The Last Supper painting — a fate Constance foreshadowed during her first meeting with Ben in the season premiere .

The Hollywood Reporter spoke with Kelly about playing the central villain of AHS: 13 , working alongside Lange, his character’s fate and whether he’d be interested in returning — or thinks Mr. Nas could return — for the already-renewed 14th season of Ryan Murphy and Brad Falchuk’s series.

When you first signed on for the season, did you know what your character’s ending would be, or when did you find out?

Oh, boy. I didn’t really know anything about how the season would go. They were writing it as we went along. I think there were maybe five episodes when I started, and there are 13 episodes in the season, so things change, things go and just play along.

Logo text He’s back, and he’s angrier than ever! Godzilla Minus Zero had a series of screenings this week for press and the first reactions have been flooding social media. The verdict? We have another kaiju-sized hit on our hands.

Despite having its world premiere at the New York Film Festival on Sept. 26, legendary Japanese studio Toho held more press screenings this week for Godzilla Minus Zero ahead of the film’s Centerpiece gala screening at the Tokyo International Film Festival on Nov. 1. The film is released in theaters in Japan on Nov. 3 and North America on Nov. 6. Written and directed by Takashi Yamazaki , Godzilla Minus Zero is a direct sequel to the Japanese filmmaker’s 2023 epic Godzilla Minus One , that scored over $100 million at the global box office from a $15 million budget and won an Oscar for best visual effects in 2024.

A synopsis from Toho of Godzilla Minus Zero reads: “War reduced Japan to zero, and Godzilla plunged it into minus. Two years have passed since then, and the country has faced agonizing struggles to achieve recovery and finally reclaim its daily life. Just as humanity managed to cling to a hard-won peace, a new threat strikes, crushing hope in an instant. There is no third time. Everything ends here.”

Ryunosuke Kamiki, Minami Hamabe, Hidetaka Yoshioka and Kuranosuke Sasaki are among the cast returning for the sequel. Newcomers include Min Tanaka and Masami Nagasawa.

Shot entirely in Japan, notably, Godzilla Minus Zero is the first-ever Japanese production to be filmed for Imax.

The Hollywood Reporter ‘s David Rooney reviewed Godzilla Minus Zero after seeing it NYFF , and described the film as a “radioactive blast.” In a rave review, Rooney praised Yamazaki for topping the spectacle of his first film. “The resulting clash of the legendary kaiju is a rip-roaring smackdown in a movie that keeps awing the audience with exhilarating action and then continually one-upping itself in the dustups that follow,” Rooney writes. “I’m fairly sure I stopped breathing during a tense scene in which Godzilla bears down on a seaplane attempting a hurried liftoff.”

Godzilla Minus Zero currently holds a score of 92 percent on Rotten Tomatoes from 50 reviews. On Metacritic it holds a score of 78 and on Letterboxd it is rated at 4 stars.

entertainment.title: ‘Final Album, Final Tour’: Ministry’s Al Jourgensen Talks ‘Hate to Go’
entertainment.summary: Ministry does not pull a single punch on "Hate To Go," which castigates social media, AI and the current political leadership of the United States.
entertainment.body:
Raise a skeptical eyebrow if you will, but Al Jourgensen will swear on any object you put him front of him that Ministry’ s new album Hate to Go (Take Out or Delivery) is its last, and that the group will be over after touring to support it next year. Explore Al Jourgensen Ministry See latest videos, charts and news

“It is so — final album, final tour. In 14 months from now I will be just a simple goat herder,” the dreadlocked Jourgensen, who founded Ministry during 1981, tells Billboard via Zoom from his current home in southern California. “I will be the Greta Garbo of industrial — ‘I vant to be left alone,’ OK? This is not like something where Motley Crue talks a blood oath they will not be back, and four months later they’re doing a world tour. I’m f***in’ done.” Related Selena Gomez Celebrates 'Ups & Downs' With Demi Lovato: 'I'm Proud of What We've Been Through' Meet Leah Barylsky, the Woman Behind the Camera - And On the Stage -- During Rüfüs Du Sol's Record-Breaking Tour Will My Chemical Romance Score Its First No. 1 Album Next Week (With a 20-Year-Old Album)?

“Look, man, I’ve been at this job for…it’ll be 45 years this year, and at 45 years of the same job generally you get a gold watch and a pension and you’re just happy to get the f*** away from your job,” says Jorgensen, 68. “I don’t understand these people that keep coming back. There’s no regrets. There’s no turning back. We’re excited for new possibilities in life instead of doing the same job for 45 years.”

There’s no question that Jourgensen and his shifting stable of collaborators have done that job well, of course. A fan of rock, punk, country and experimental styles, Jourgensen started Ministry after a tenure in the post-punk band Special Affect, introducing the new band’s dance-floor meets factory forge sound with singles on Chicago’s famed Wax Trax! Records label and making its live performance debut on New Year’s Day 1982. A deal with Arista Records, however, resulted in the sanitized synth-pop of With Sympathy in 1983. “Clive Davis didn’t want that (heavy stuff),” recalls Jourgensen, who redid many of those songs on Ministry’s 2025 album The Squirrely Years. “He appointed producers, backup singers. He even sent in lyrics that I had to sing and all that stuff — so I was literally probably the precursor to all the boy band stuff. The only thing I didn’t have was dance moves.”

Jourgensen regained control by moving to Sire Records for 1986’s Twitch and progressed from there on subsequent, definitive albums such as The Land of Rape and Honey in 1988, The Mind is a Terrible Thing to Taste in 1990, the platinum Psalm 69 in 1992 — which netted the first of Ministry’s six Grammy Award nominations for the opening track, “N.W.O.” — and the 1996’s Filth Pig , which peaked at No. 19 on the Billboard 200. Angst-filled and politically pointed, Ministry became a vanguard of industrial rock, with Jourgensen as majordomo, launching side projects such as Revolting Cocks and Lard and providing the groundwork for the all-star collective Pigface.

TeamLab , the Japanese digital art collective famous for its immersive exhibitions, is set to open its first permanent space in the U.S.

On Thursday, Bloomberg reported that the Samueli family, the billionaire owners of NHL team the Anaheim Mighty Ducks, had struck a more than $100 million deal with TeamLab to open a space in Anaheim, California that is projected to open in 2030. The space will be part of a larger $5 billion development of the land surrounding the Ducks’ home the Honda Center.

TeamLab will be a key component of the OCVIBE development that is converting about 100 acres of land into a multiuse area, with housing, offices, hotels and an entertainment district. Bloomberg reported that the development of TeamLab Anaheim will be fully funded by the Samueli family. TeamLab Anaheim will be housed in a building designed by California-based architecture firm Smith-Clementi. Related Stories Movies Tokyo: Finecut Inks Deals for Justin H. Min's 'Journey There,' Hong Sangsoo's 'Nowhere to Lay My Eyes' Movies Patrick Stewart, 'Star Trek' Captain and 'X-Men' Superhero, Dies at 86

Founded in Tokyo in 2001 by Toshiyuki Inoko, TeamLab is an international art collective, made up of a multi-disciplinary team, including artists, programmers, engineers, CG animators, mathematicians, and architects who collaborate to explore the intersection of art, science, technology, and nature.

TeamLab Anaheim will be 30 miles south of Los Angeles, and about a 10-minute drive from Disneyland. The developers will be hoping it will be as popular and pop culturally relevant as other TeamLab spaces around the world. According to TeamLab, the collective’s two locations in Tokyo had over 4.2 million visitors in 2025. entertainment.title: Patrick Stewart’s Career Was a Rare and Thrilling Marriage of the Prestigious and the Populist
entertainment.summary: Stewart's classical theater chops invested genre film and television roles with unlikely dramatic weight, psychological depth and piercing feeling.
entertainment.body:
In the first two decades and change of Patrick Stewart’s distinguished professional career , he spent 16 years with the Royal Shakespeare Company, made his Broadway debut alongside Ben Kingsley and Frances de la Tour in a legendary production of A Midsummer Night’s Dream directed by influential theater giant Peter Brook, and became a frequent presence on the storied stages of the prestigious Royal National Theatre.

It’s a telling insight into the hermetically sealed bubble of Hollywood that a renowned classical actor with years of notable work behind him, when cast in 1987 in the sci-fi TV spin-off Star Trek: The Next Generation , was identified in the Los Angeles Times as an “unknown British Shakespearean actor.” Stewart, who died Wednesday at 86, now runs no risk of being called unknown. Related Stories Movies Ian McKellen Pays Tribute to Patrick Stewart: "A Man to Rely on, Admire and in My Case, Love" Movies Patrick Stewart Rose From Obscurity to Boldly (and Baldly) Go Where No Yorkshireman Had Gone Before

That wealth of stage experience was deeply embedded in his layered characterization as Captain Jean-Luc Picard, commander of the USS Enterprise, allowing Stewart to project steely authority without ever losing sight of the man’s kindness and compassion, his mentorship and familial protectiveness toward his crew.

While longtime friend and colleague Ian McKellen urged him not to toss away his prime Shakespeare years — the trajectory that ideally leads from Hamlet and Macbeth all the way to King Lear — Stewart took the Star Trek job. He signed the standard six-year contract despite quiet assurances from his agents and other industry associates that the show would likely last a single season, after which he could pocket his television earnings and return to his first love, the British stage.

But the spacetime continuum has a way of scrambling well-made plans. Not only did the show run for 178 episodes over seven seasons — peaking at 12 million viewers until the 1994 series finale, which was watched by more than 30 million — it also spawned four feature films, plus an additional spinoff, Star Trek: Picard , for which Stewart returned to the role for a three-season run.

The endlessly regenerative sci-fi phenomenon made Stewart a wealthy man and gave him global recognition, but by all accounts, the rigorous discipline he had acquired over all those years treading the boards was instrumental in shaping the work ethic of the entire company. As Picard, he also played a decisive role in making bald sexy.
