Ian McKellen is paying tribute to Patrick Stewart following news of his death at 86.

Stewart died Wednesday at his home in Los Angeles following “a brief and poignant journey with Alzheimer’s disease and Lewy body dementia,” longtime spokesperson Kelly Bush Novak announced.

“He has been held in the warm embrace of family and friends, surrounded by live music, prayer, tears, laughter and the kind of profound emotion that only he could inspire after a lifetime of devotion to us all,” Bush Novak wrote. “We will forever cherish the peaceful ease and reflection on his face, an enduring reminder of his invincible grace.” Related Stories Movies Jamie Dornan Boards 'Nostalgie,' Starring Aidan Gillen as Washed-up Pop Star, as Executive Producer (Exclusive) Movies 'Godzilla Minus Zero': First Reactions

The Oscar nominee shared a tribute on his social media platforms on Thursday, writing, “Before everything else, Patrick was defined by being born and bred in Yorkshire, the proud county in the north of England which he loved to the end. You could hear it in his accented voice and in the stern honesty with which he told you what he thought and felt. Yorkshiremen have no truck with half-truths or avoidance of big issues. He wore his heart on his sleeve, which made him a man to rely on, to admire and in my case, love.”

“We first met as ambitious young actors with the Royal Shakespeare Company half a century ago but we weren’t in the same productions. My first strong memory was a few years later, meeting him in the street in central London when he told me about an offer to take over a leading part in Star Trek ,” he wrote. “‘But Patrick think of your stage career in the U.K. Do you really want to risk — getting lost in Hollywood for years and years?’ Well, he took the risk and thank goodness for us all that he did for not just his devoted Trekkies but film and theatre audiences, who marvelled at his using international celebrity to star in a string of cinema successes ( X-Men of course) and in great classical plays by Shakespeare, Ibsen, Arthur Miller, Peter Shaffer, Pinter and Beckett at Stratford-upon-Avon, in London’s West End and on Broadway.”

McKellen and Stewart led the original X-Men franchise for 20th Century Fox, portraying Magneto/Erik Lehnsherr and Professor Charles Xavier, respectively. Their characters were infamous rivals who forged a friendship, with the latter being true of their off-screen relationship. The two will reprise their X-Men roles in Marvel’s upcoming Avengers: Doomsday this December.

entertainment.title: Mary J. Blige Puts Booing Heckler on Blast During Las Vegas Residency Concert: ‘The F–k You Spend Your Money for, Idiot?’
entertainment.summary: The Queen of Hip-Hop Soul's My Life, My Story residency continues on Friday (Oct. 30).
entertainment.body:
Mary J. Blige is not one to be played with. The Queen of Hip-Hop Soul put a booing heckler on blast during Wednesday night’s (Oct. 28) concert of her My Life, My Story Las Vegas residency.

“To the b—h that’s booing, you didn’t have to come here,” Blige said to the fan — as captured by TMZ — in the midst of her show at Sin City’s Dolby Live at Park MGM. “I hope someone sees you and politely removes you.”

The R&B icon continued to slam the heckler and apologized to the crowd for the disruption, blaming her Yonkers roots for clapping back and putting an end to the nonsense.

“The f–k you spend your money for, idiot?” she piled on. “I’m sorry. Sometimes I have to go in because that’s where I’m from.”

Mary J. Blige got back to performing as usual and continued the show like nothing took place. Shortly after, the 55-year-old brought out Wyclef Jean as a special guest to perform their top 40 Billboard Hot 100 hit “911.”

Blige will return to the stage on Friday (Oct. 30) with a second weekend show on tap for Halloween at Dolby Live, which is the Grammy-winning singer’s last residency date of 2026. The My Life, My Story residency will conclude in 2027 with five dates in February.

“This residency felt like divine timing,” the Rock and Roll Hall of Famer said in a statement in September when the ending of the residency was revealed. “I’ve seen so many of you in Vegas and we still have 10 dates left. I feel even more grateful and deeply inspired after every show. Grab your girlfriends, your boots, and I’ll see you in Vegas in October and February.”

Blige’s last album, Gratitude , arrived in November 2024. It marked her first studio LP not to make the Billboard 200 .
